data.title: First Merchants Issues New Subordinated Notes Offering
data.description:
First Merchants ( (FRME) ) has issued an update.

First Merchants Corporation entered into an indenture and first supplemental indenture with U.S. Bank Trust Company, National Association, on September 25, 2026, to issue $100 million of 6.750% fixed-to-floating rate subordinated notes due October 1, 2036. The notes pay a fixed 6.750% semi-annual coupon until October 1, 2031, then convert to a floating rate tied to a benchmark expected to be Three-Month Term SOFR plus 202 basis points, with a zero floor, and may be redeemed at par plus accrued interest starting October 1, 2031 or earlier upon specified regulatory, tax, or investment company events.

The issuance was conducted under an effective shelf registration statement, supporting First Merchants’ ability to access capital markets and structure instruments that can qualify as Tier 2 capital, subject to Federal Reserve rules. The detailed redemption provisions linked to tax treatment, regulatory capital status, and investment company registration underscore the company’s intent to preserve regulatory capital treatment while retaining flexibility to retire the notes if their regulatory or tax profile changes, impacting investors’ call risk and the timing of potential redemptions.

data.title: Maisons du Monde tightens costs and cleans up balance sheet as sales slide
data.description:
An announcement from Maisons du Monde SA ( (FR:MDM) ) is now available.

Maisons du Monde reported first‑half 2026 net sales of €412.8 million, down 7.1% year‑on‑year amid a sluggish home furnishings market and constrained inventory levels, with sharper declines in online activity and weaker performance in Germany and Austria. Despite a deeper current EBIT loss of €36.8 million and a gross margin contraction, the group delivered €15 million in cost savings, improved working capital through inventory reductions, and narrowed its net loss to €64 million.

Free cash flow remained negative at €49.8 million but improved versus 2025, while operating costs fell 4.8% thanks to logistics and transport efficiencies, partly offset by inflation and IT‑related transformation costs. Following a comprehensive refinancing completed in July, pro forma net financial debt was cut to €24.6 million, leaving the company with a cleaned‑up balance sheet and greater financial stability to pursue its turnaround and long‑term profitability objectives under the backing of new shareholders.

data.title: Moleculin Highlights Immune-Driven Annamycin Pancreatic Cancer Data
data.description:
Moleculin Biotech ( (MBRX) ) has provided an update.

On September 25, 2026, Moleculin Biotech reported new preclinical data showing that its lead drug Annamycin (naxtarubicin) exerts antitumor activity in pancreatic cancer partly through CD8+ T cell cytotoxicity. The data, presented at the AACR Conference on Pancreatic Cancer in San Diego, suggest Annamycin may help convert immunologically “cold” pancreatic tumors into “hot” tumors that are more susceptible to immune attack.

Because pancreatic cancer’s cold immune microenvironment has limited the effectiveness of checkpoint inhibitors, the evidence of an immune-mediated component to Annamycin’s activity highlights potential for future combination strategies and scientific alignment with Moleculin’s immune-modulating WP1066 program. The findings remain confined to preclinical models and are not part of the ongoing MIRACLE trial in acute myeloid leukemia, so they do not immediately alter Moleculin’s clinical focus but could broaden the long-term therapeutic scope of Annamycin if similar effects are demonstrated in humans.
